tactic.scheme: The pattern of T-tac-ladder-dual, one more two-sided node: hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_of_dual : C.dual.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere → C.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (safe forward), hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_dual : C.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere → C.dual.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (safe forward, pattern Causality.dual C), each `.1`/`.2` of Causality.dual_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:121). The node is one-sided only in that one side suffices at each point (I⁺(p) or I⁻(p) non-empty), so it is invariant under time reversal and is transported both ways like the other two-sided nodes, unlike causally_open_future (DEC-163).
tactic.termination: Unchanged: the pair is a one-causality rule pair, so it writes t.dual only for a t.dual already in sight (the pattern) and creates no new reversal. Every negative fails by exhaustive search (below).
tactic.curvesExtend_dual_iff: Now `⟨CurvesExtend.dual (C := C.dual), CurvesExtend.dual⟩`: .1 is Causality.CurvesExtend.dual at C.dual, whose conclusion C.dual.dual.CurvesExtend is C.CurvesExtend by rfl (Causality.dual_dual), .2 is it at C. The 12-line re-proof (kb/0248) is gone; the rule wrappers curvesExtend_of_dual / curvesExtend_dual are untouched.

aesop_could_not: The unfolded form is not read across time reversal: (h : ∀ p, C.HasChronalNeighbour p) ⊢ C.dual.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere fails by exhaustion (a hypothesis whose type is not reducibly the node matches no forward rule; enableUnfold is off). On C itself it closes, by the builtin assumption up to definitional unfolding.

The point predicate has no rule: (h : C.HasChronalNeighbour p) ⊢ C.dual.HasChronalNeighbour p fails by exhaustion (Causality.dual_hasChronalNeighbour, Causal.LocateExtension, is not a node and has no wrapper). From the node it works: C.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere ⊢ C.dual.HasChronalNeighbour p closes, the node transported and then applied at p by aesop's builtin applyHyps (apply unfolds the definition to its ∀). So Lemma 2.17's boundary hypothesis (HasChronalNeighbour on ∂O) is reached from the node, not from a pointwise hypothesis.

NonemptyChronalCones is not a node: (h : C.NonemptyChronalCones) ⊢ C.dual.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (or the same on C) fails; NonemptyChronalCones.hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere is no rule (the keeper's choice in programme/ladder.toml: one node, not two).

T-tac-dual-generated: dual_closure.py now refuses to run when Dual.lean lacks the pair of a two-sided node, which is the check emit-lean would make if it generated Dual.lean; the naming rule it uses (p_of_dual / p_dual with p the node's Lean name, first letter lowered) holds for all 17 two-sided nodes, so emit-lean can generate the wrappers from a [[property]] key `dual` naming the iff (Causal.Causality.dual_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere here) with no hand-chosen names. A new causality-sort node that is not invariant under time reversal must then be marked one-sided in the ladder (the script's ONE_SIDED).

A point-predicate rule (C.HasChronalNeighbour p → C.dual.HasChronalNeighbour p, pattern on C.dual) would close the pointwise form of Lemma 2.17's boundary hypothesis across reversal. Not added: the point predicate is not a node (the ladder keeps it an edge hypothesis, in words), and DualTest models nodes only.
